title: What rebalancing does and doesn't do
objectives: State four things rebalancing does and four it doesn't.
Explain why a rebalanced portfolio can end with less in a strong rally.
body_md:
Key point: the main job of rebalancing is risk control. In a strongly rising market, a rebalanced portfolio can end up with less than one left alone, because it keeps trimming equity. That is the price of keeping risk where the client wants it.

| It does | It doesn't |
| --- | --- |
| Keep risk at the level the client agreed to | Guarantee higher returns |
| Make the client sell some of what has risen and buy what has fallen, by rule | Predict markets or time the top and bottom |
| Remove emotion from buying and selling decisions | Come free: selling can mean exit loads and tax |
| Make falls easier to sit through | Replace a review of the goal itself |
example: In a strong rally, trimming equity keeps risk at the agreed level — but it also means giving up some of the rally. That is the price, not a failure.
say: The main job of rebalancing is risk control.
Rebalancing doesn't predict markets or time the top and bottom.
